newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Tulip in red as computer sales fail to bloom.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Tulip in red as computer sales fail to bloom.

text.p: Tulip Computers, the only Dutch personal computer maker, on Monday posted a net loss of almost 10 million guilders for 1996 compared with a profit of 9.2 million guilders in 1995.
But the company, which announced last year that for the first time it planned to share part of its profits with employees in 1996, forecast a profit for the current year.
"We expect a positive result for the full-year of 1997. But we have to warn that the first half of 1997 might not yet result in a profit," director Franz Hetzenauer told a news conference.
Tulip, a niche player in the personal computer market, said turnover was somewhat disappointing in 1996, slipping to 528 million guilders from 532 million guilders a year earlier.
Sales to other European manufacturers who sell Tulip computers under their own label fell by 63 percent in 1996.
But Hetzenauer was more upbeat about coming years, saying the European market for computers was expected to grow by an average of more than 15 percent.
Tulip also added that sales in Europe of computers with its own brand name rose by 16.5 percent in 1996.
Tulip recently moved to a new Dutch plant with an annual production capacity of 600,000 units near the southern city of Den Bosch.
The company, which failed in its intention to link up with an unnamed partner last December, said it was still considering an alliance with another firm.
"We would consider a strategic alliance with a partner if this would have a positive impact for Tulip," it said.
Hetzenauer said this meant it would have to make a positive impact on sales, margins or distribution. He declined to explain why the intended alliance had failed last year.
"We believe in our own strength," Hetzenauer said, adding he would look very carefully if new candidates turned up.
